WITH q AS (SELECT estimator_id e, substr(sent_on,1,7) ym, (status='won')::int w FROM erp_quotes WHERE kind='new' AND status IS NOT NULL AND status<>''),
cell AS (SELECT ym,e,count(*) n,sum(w) w FROM q GROUP BY 1,2),
tot AS (SELECT ym,sum(n) n,sum(w) w FROM cell GROUP BY 1),
j AS (SELECT cell.*, tot.n-cell.n on_, tot.w-cell.w ow FROM cell JOIN tot USING(ym) WHERE tot.n>cell.n)
SELECT e, sum(n) n, round((sum(w)-sum(n*ow/on_))/sum(n),3) diff FROM j WHERE e IN (108,109,115,254,327) GROUP BY e ORDER BY e

content.text:
I accepted the challenge and saved the revised `finding.json` with `"accepted": true`. I re-ran the key query myself (q334) and got the challenger's numbers again: quoter 115 is -0.031, estimator 109 is -0.038 and estimator 108 is +0.033.

**What changed:**
- **The comparison was flawed.** I compared 115's quotes with other quoters' quotes to the same customer in the same year. That set 115's quotes from the worst months of 2021 against peers' quotes from better months. Comparing only with quotes from the same calendar month halves the gap to -0.031 (n=430). Allowing for quotes to the same customer being related, that is about 1.8 standard errors, which isn't conventionally significant (q290, q312).
- **115 is not an estimator.** HR lists 115 as an engineer who is still employed. Half of 115's new quotes (217 of 430) fall in 14 months, mostly right after estimators or other quoters left. In those months the other quoters won 0.187, against 0.272 in months when 115 didn't quote (q276, q299, q300).
- **115 isn't singled out any more.** Matched by month, 115's gap is about the same as full-time estimator 109's. The difference between estimators 108 and 109 (0.071) is larger than 115's gap. In 2021 115 won at the same rate as peers that month: 0.125 against an expected 0.119 (q315, q320).
- **The dollar figure drops** from $33,837 to $20,872 a year (q312). That is the value of the quotes, not margin. Much of it built up when no estimator was available to send those quotes instead, so it isn't money the shop could have recovered.
- **The headline is now about estimating coverage.** When an estimator leaves, quoting falls to non-estimators and slows down. Slower quotes win less even compared with quotes from the same month: +0.078 for 0–2 days against -0.092 for 8–30 days (q317). That is still a correlation, since slow quotes may be the harder requests.

**What I added or kept:**
- Three of the 14 busy months for 115 (2019-12, 2022-12, 2023-08) don't follow anyone leaving, so departures explain most of the pattern, not all of it.
- A smaller gap of -0.049 outside 2021 remains, at about 2 standard errors (q305). It leans on 2022, when 115 won 2 of 37 quotes (q315). I report it but don't treat it as a solid pattern for one person.
- Price, quote size and how quote statuses were recorded still don't explain the gap (q248, q279, q283, q286).

Confidence stays medium.
